title: Sidewalk Toronto / Quayside
domain: urban development, data governance, public-private partnership
research_role: hard case for standing, public authority and data rights
case_selection_rationale: A bilateral development relation proposed rules with public externalities; it reveals when parties to a contract are not the only entities with legitimate standing.

initial_relation_frame.R: Waterfront Toronto, Sidewalk Labs, three levels of government, expert panel, public/affected communities, future development partners.
initial_relation_frame.V: Master plan, land development, digital proposals, data governance, public benefit, IP, approvals.
initial_relation_frame.T: Proposal → consultation/evaluation → threshold resolution → board/government approvals or refusal → implementation agreements or termination.
initial_relation_frame.A: Waterfront Toronto and Sidewalk approvals; public-sector/government authority over privacy, digital governance and land/public-interest decisions.
initial_relation_frame.E: Public consultation, technical evaluation, expert review, legal/regulatory compliance and future project readbacks.
initial_relation_frame.D: Collection, localization, governance, use and public value of urban data; IP and co-created assets.
initial_relation_frame.O: Pursue all/some/none; staged approvals; implementation agreements; withdrawal/termination.

powers: law, land, planning, privacy and regulatory approvals
standing to challenge and shape public-interest evaluation; not identical to bilateral signature authority
independent expert challenge/advice; no final approval

timeline.label: Plan Development Agreement creates a staged relation
timeline.description: The agreement defines the parties, approvals, development process and multiple termination conditions rather than treating the project as a simple purchase.
timeline.authority_effect: Creates bilateral approval and exit authority.
timeline.outcome_effect: Creates a formal formation process, not final implementation.

timeline.label: Draft MIDP expands the proposed relation
timeline.description: The draft plan introduces broad land, governance, data, IP and implementation proposals beyond a narrow parameter negotiation.
timeline.authority_effect: Proposes new governance and implementation roles.
timeline.outcome_effect: Starts public/technical evaluation rather than producing acceptance.

timeline.label: Public consultation challenges scope, governance, consent and data proposals
timeline.description: Public feedback objects to scope overreach, unclear democratic control, surveillance/consent, IP and missing public-benefit evidence.
timeline.authority_effect: Demonstrates that affected stakeholders have claims not reducible to the two contracting parties.

timeline.label: Threshold resolution reallocates authority and constrains data governance
timeline.description: Waterfront Toronto becomes the lead for privacy/digital governance and government discussions; public consultation, Canadian storage and public-sector control replace or constrain parts of the original proposal.
timeline.authority_effect: Moves key governance authority away from the private proposer and requires broader approval.
timeline.outcome_effect: Produces a narrower, conditionally viable relation version.

timeline.label: Expert panel accepts improvement but finds critical details unresolved
timeline.description: The expert review reports that the revised appendix is materially improved while a fully realized digital-governance framework and other critical details remain absent.
timeline.authority_effect: Blocks silent conversion of a partial resolution into public acceptance.
timeline.outcome_effect: Keeps the relation in conditional/unknown state.

timeline.label: Sidewalk Labs terminates the PDA
timeline.description: The contractual relation is terminated. Official reporting attributes withdrawal to unprecedented economic uncertainty arising from COVID-19; governance disputes cannot be asserted as the cause of termination.
timeline.authority_effect: Exercises a valid exit path; surviving IP/data/confidentiality provisions remain.
timeline.outcome_effect: Outcome is WITHDRAWN, not rejected on a proved governance cause.

operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.operation: Extensive plan development, consultation and threshold negotiation occurred; no full project implementation.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.effect: Formal governance/scope terms changed and the development agreement was terminated.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.adoption: Waterfront Toronto reports retaining planning insights; the Quayside proposal itself was not adopted.
operation_effect_adoption_acceptance.acceptance: No final multi-authority acceptance of the project. Public/expert positions remained heterogeneous.

supports: Material relation change can be driven by authority, standing, data rights and effect rules rather than price or scope alone.
Bilateral recognition is insufficient when third parties bear public externalities or possess public-law authority.
Independent challenge can produce a real Design Delta without producing a final deal.
A valid negative disposition and exit path are part of a truthful coordination system.
does_not_support: It does not show that Towow or Agent mediation would have improved the project.
It does not show that governance conflict caused termination.
It does not establish the private preferences or complete internal worlds of either party.
competing_explanations: The threshold changes could be ordinary public procurement/governance correction rather than evidence for a new A2A-specific mechanism.
The project may have remained commercially infeasible regardless of governance improvements.
Published consultation records overrepresent views that entered official channels.
design_delta: Add affected-party standing and representation to R/A; signature authority and legitimate challenge rights are distinct.
Compile readiness for public-impact relations must include a legitimacy/standing closure, not only bilateral Mandates.
Do not infer causal failure from a material unresolved issue when the recorded termination cause is different.
Exit can preserve selected rights/knowledge; WITHDRAWN is not equivalent to erasing the relation history.
unknowns: What exact terms would have passed final boards/governments

chronology_preserving_diagnostic.subsequent_observed_change: Threshold resolution changed the same authority/data/scope dimensions; this is chronology-consistent but not a blinded prediction.
chronology_preserving_diagnostic.gate_interpretation: A v0.4-style compile gate should have remained closed before threshold resolution and again where DSAP identified unresolved material details.
